note: The known-failure set: persisted Bucket B classifications, one entry per expected failure, keyed by assertion name plus target. Checked in deliberately - it is not derived from a previous run, because a run cannot be its own authority. It ratchets both ways: a failure absent from this file is new and blocks; an entry that stops failing is stale and must be removed deliberately, since an expected failure that quietly disappeared is either a fix worth recording or a test that stopped running. Neither direction may be resolved by the harness on its own. See evals/HARNESS.md.

failures.assertion: Repository shape.exercises the exported command Get-PSModuleAssembly somewhere in tests
failures.reason: Get-PSModuleAssembly is exported but no test invokes it. Its only appearance in the test tree is a string literal in the export list in tests/Module.Quality.Tests.ps1, which asserts the command is exported, not that it works.

failures.assertion: Manifest.exports no cmdlets, variables, or aliases implicitly
failures.reason: VariablesToExport is absent from the manifest. An unset export key defaults to a wildcard, so the module does leak.

failures.assertion: Manifest.exports no cmdlets, variables, or aliases implicitly
failures.reason: VariablesToExport is commented out at manifest line 115, so the key is absent and defaults to a wildcard.

Manifest.exports no cmdlets, variables, or aliases implicitly
failures.reason: All three export keys absent - three failing cases of one assertion.

failures.assertion: Manifest.exports no cmdlets, variables, or aliases implicitly
failures.reason: Sets an export key to '*' outright rather than omitting it. Explicit rather than implicit, and still a wildcard export.

failures.assertion: Public surface.defines every function the manifest exports somewhere in source
failures.reason: Export-ExcelSheet and Invoke-AllTests are listed in FunctionsToExport but are [Alias()] names on other functions, not functions. The manifest exports an alias as though it were a function.

failures.assertion: Public surface.gives <_.Name> comment-based help with a synopsis
failures.reason: 60 exported functions carry no comment-based help and the module ships no external help directory. Get-Help on them returns nothing useful.

failures.assertion: Public surface.gives <_.Name> comment-based help with a synopsis
failures.reason: 10 of 13 exported functions undocumented. The module's psm1 contains three .SYNOPSIS blocks in total.

failures.assertion: Public surface.gives <_.Name> comment-based help with a synopsis
failures.reason: Expand-GitCommand, Get-PromptPath, Update-AllBranches, TabExpansion and tgit are exported without comment-based help. posh-git documents 20 functions this way, so the omission is inconsistency rather than a project-wide convention. This is the only assertion the corpus control still fails, and it fails for a real reason - see the note in UNIVERSAL-CORPUS.md.
